title: Cross-tenant memory entanglement causing intermittent GPU OOMs and degraded throughput
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
A cluster of hosted and Dedicated nodes experienced recurring GPU OOMs during long-tail prompt workloads. Investigation shows memory pressure stems from a subtle interaction between the KV prefix cache and the global slab allocator: repeated small allocations plus KV tombstone retention produce severe fragmentation and cross-tenant arena reuse that prevents effective reclamation. The result is an intermittent cascade: tenant A triggers sustained KV growth, allocator fails to coalesce freed spans, tenant B receives allocations from fragmented arenas and hits OOM despite overall cluster capacity.

Impact:
- Affected customers: 3 hosted tenants and 1 Dedicated customer reported generation failures and elevated latency.
- Symptoms: p95/p99 latency spikes, token generation errors with OOM traces, increased GPU memory high-water marks.
- Customer impact: high; one customer escalated (SEV2) after production failures.

Root cause (hypothesis validated by heap captures and KV telemetry):
1) KV prefix cache creates many short-lived small allocations that populate slab classes unevenly.
2) Tombstone metadata for evicted KV entries was not compacted promptly; tombstone growth kept slots logically dead but physically reserved.
3) The global allocator occasionally reuses arenas across tenants without clearing per-tenant metadata, producing cross-tenant pointer retention (memory entanglement).
4) Under heavy long-tail prompting (many short contexts and rerank requests) fragmentation reached a tipping point and continuous allocations failed, producing GPU OOMs.

Short-term mitigations completed (actions taken):
- Isolated affected hosted tenants by migrating traffic to dedicated warm pools (manual move) to stop cross-tenant pressure (completed 2026-03-02 04:30 UTC).
- Applied temporary runtime knob to disable KV prefix caching for heavy tenants (feature flag rolled out to 4 nodes) to reduce small-allocation churn (completed 2026-03-02 09:00 UTC).
- Emergency throttle: added a soft rate limiter per-tenant to cap concurrent stream handoffs on impacted nodes (deployed 2026-03-02 14:00 UTC).
- Coordinated support messages and credits with Customer Success for the SEV2 tenant (acknowledged and assigned remediation engineer).

Short-term patch (in-progress):
- Patch PR adds an aggressive KV tombstone sweeper that runs as part of the eviction path and forces slot reclamation for categories showing >T tombstones. Also adds a safety mem-accounting backstop to fail allocations gracefully before OOM and trigger proactive evict/compaction. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1476 (in review).
- Canary scheduled to roll to 10% of affected pools (staging canary passed). Monitoring hooks added for tombstone_count, frag_ratio, allocator_reuse_rate, and OOM_count.

Long-term design work (next quarter):
- Introduce per-tenant arenas to eliminate cross-tenant pointer retention and enable targeted compaction without global pauses.
- Implement a compact-on-idle policy in the allocator to proactively defragment slabs with high fragmentation metrics.
- Rework KV metadata layout to reduce tombstone footprint and support incremental compaction.
- Add a suite of long-tail prompt unit and stress tests that reproduce small-allocation churn and guardrails in CI.

Rollout plan for short-term patch (detailed):
- Stage -> internal staging cluster (passed functional + mem snapshot validation) -> canary 10% prod (1-day observation) -> 30% (12h observation) -> full rollout.
- Metrics to watch during canary: OOM_count, p99_latency, tombstone_count, frag_ratio, allocated_bytes_by_tenant, model-throughput.
- Rollback if OOM_count increases > 50% vs baseline or p99 latency regresses > 20% sustained for 30m.
- Owners: Aisha Kumar (engineering lead), Miguel Ortega (runtime owner), Priya Patel (on-call escalation liaison).

Next steps and open work items:
- Finish code review and perf validation for PR #1476 (target merge: 2026-03-06).
- Run extended soak test against synthetic long-tail prompt workload for 48h post-merge.
- Draft Confluence runbook for tenant isolation and migration steps so Support can perform rapid mitigation.
- Schedule architecture spike for per-tenant arenas (estimate: 3 sprints).

Notes on reproducibility and artifacts:
- Heap captures, allocator traces, and KV telemetry for the incident uploaded to: https://drive.company.internal/incident/ENG-582019/heap_traces.zip
- Incident Slack channel: #inc-582019-memory-entanglement
- Customer-facing incident summary: https://confluence.company.internal/incident/ENG-582019-summary
